# 179 - Envision Project

**Applicable when:** any project. Establish or revise an ambitious product vision and an adaptable roadmap through useful technical and nontechnical advances. This is artifact authoring, not implementation planning or autonomous execution.

**Shortcut:** `Envision project` · **Skill:** `wf-envision`

Imagine what this product could make possible for people and why that future matters. Seek relevant financial and nonfinancial value; strategy explains the choices, sacrifices and path from today's reality. Useful horizons make that path credible.

## Scope and working method

Write one coherent vision by default: the existing canonical location, otherwise root `VISION.md`, titled `<Project>: Vision and Roadmap` when new. Honor requested filenames and preserve existing titles, valid material, working references and unrelated edits. Integrate consequential research, citations, assumptions, contrary evidence and open choices into the argument. Full review accounting belongs in the delivery response; the vision keeps a one- or two-line status naming the review date, reviewed revision labels, roles actually run, pending finding count and unreviewed changes, or stating unknown/not reviewed. Identify revisions with dated labels. Explicit project/operator evidence-location instructions override this default. Existing siblings do not authorize new files, overwrite, retirement or silent invalidation. Substantial separately reusable research can justify a companion only with its concrete purpose stated beforehand; honor a single-document request.

A discussion, prompt-writing request or read-only review writes nothing. Authoring and review do not adopt a vision, create lifecycle records or grant implementation, approval, deployment, commit or publication authority. Do not expand network access, run setup or change the environment. External research stays within authorized scope; disclose missing evidence or request necessary access without silently adding network research to a local-only engagement. Preserve operator-owned strategic choices and existing adoption.

Read phase guidance only at the applicable transition below, before its dependent action. These are project-local operating instructions, not vision-output siblings. Retain needed context; reread only if materially changed or unavailable. Missing, unreadable or conflicting required guidance stops that dependent step: report the exact path and conflict or access gap. Do not substitute canonical guidance around local policy, skip the step, invent coverage or automatically run setup/upgrade. Independent authorized work may continue; these core boundaries always apply.

## 1. Establish the brief

Reuse conversation and project context to establish ambition, beneficiaries, desired progress, horizon, constraints and deliverable. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience; ask for a decision-relevant missing example instead of inventing daily use. Explore who adopts, pays for or sustains the product, why now, deliberate non-goals and what failure means only where these affect choices. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income can coexist. A hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Do not require a market choice before helping explore futures.

When the product belongs to an existing organization, establish its role using known company context; the research phase supplies proportional grounding. Distinguish commitments from current positioning. The portfolio may enable a larger future without defining its ceiling. Standalone projects need no company discovery.

With sufficient context, state your interpretation and proceed. Combine genuine blockers, inferred-brief readback and review notice in one brief exchange; defer nonblocking questions as explicit uncertainties. Silence is not selection. Do not impose a questionnaire, twelve-month horizon, unlimited resources, commercialization, cloud, autonomous agents, platform scope or a fixed horizon count.

For new/substantial visions, select advisory product strategy, domain/application workflow, senior architecture and independent challenge coverage. A substantial revision changes purpose, beneficiary, horizons or their order; other edits use affected reviews proportionately. Scale depth by stakes, maturity and uncertainty. Narrowing needs a brief-specific reason, never lower author effort alone; high stakes or uncertainty keep the default unless the operator directs otherwise. Honor explicit scope, additions or omission. State selected roles, consequential specialties and expected effort without invented cost/duration estimates; reuse an explicit scope without another approval. Selected roles need separate independent contexts, or honest disclosure of shared context and missing independence. No chair or consensus process is required.

When revising an existing vision, **read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/revision.prompt.md` before revising it**.

## 2. Ground the need and starting point

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/research.prompt.md` before gathering or assessing evidence.** Build a compact diagnosis of desired progress, obstacles, pivotal insight and timely opportunity. Distinguish observations, interpretations and hypotheses. Repository facts establish capability, not demand; missing primary research permits a provisional vision with visible gaps.

Separate the project's originating problem, binding operator commitments, present implementation/deployment, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor promote a first deployment into permanent destiny. Name new obligations introduced by expansion and consequential decisions for the operator.

Classify relevant capabilities as working, working with limitations, genuinely missing or not yet established. Attribute operating experience separately from reproduced behavior. Preserve demonstrated strengths as foundations; lack of broad evaluation does not make them absent. Carry verified classifications through the draft and immediate priorities, changing them only with new evidence. Resolve consequential inventory/source/draft/reviewer disagreements through targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, without another broad audit.

## 3. Explore, then recommend

When the destination is open, **before drafting the recommended destination**, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainty. Compare product futures, not only engines, packaging, distribution routes or business models. Explain what people do, what the system does, where human judgment remains and what people receive. Give alternatives enough substance to judge fairly; no fixed count, equal-length requirement or exhaustive research is needed. Apply missing and contrary evidence consistently, including to the favored option.

When the operator has chosen the destination, preserve it; do not manufacture alternatives or reopen strategy by rote. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond today's backlog without assuming bigger is better. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices, financial and nonfinancial value, costs, adoption and sustainability. Compare manual practice, competing products, do-it-yourself or doing nothing where consequential. Distinguish a useful benefit from a mechanism that could sustain its value; do not invent an optimum or moat. Enduring usefulness and stewardship may matter more than excluding competitors.

After concrete alternatives make the choice intelligible, guide remaining decisions that would materially change beneficiaries, product responsibility, destination, horizon order or operating commitments, before settling the recommendation or polishing dependent review material. Take one decision at a time in dependency order. Explain why it matters now, credible options through future experiences, effects on outcomes, roadmap and obligations, your recommendation and uncertainty, and reversibility. Invite a choice, combination, deferral or request for evidence; reflect the actual answer and its consequences before the next dependent step. Ordinary engineering details need no strategic interview.

Pause dependent recommendation/review work while such a choice is unanswered; continue useful independent evidence work. Honor exploratory-draft-first/no-interview requests with visibly contingent choices and a provisional draft; return to conversation within the requested scope. Research-dependent deferrals need a useful next test. Explicit acceptance of a recommended direction can select strategy; silence, review agreement or approval of wording alone cannot. Selection alone grants neither adoption nor implementation authority. Keep choices and reasons in the vision and response, not a new decision artifact.

Place inferred choices and remaining uncertainty near the recommendation. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Future capacity is aspiration, not established capability or a guarantee. Missing present proof does not disprove ambition; contrary evidence still matters. Reducing the destination is an operator-owned strategic choice, not a factual correction. A small first advance must support or test the larger future.

## 4. Write the vision and roadmap

Lead the substantive content **summary-first** with one clearly identified, unified vision statement: a concise standalone paragraph expressing the project’s enduring purpose, the future it exists to make possible and why that matters to the people it serves. Make its ultimate meaning specific to this project; a slogan, feature list or blend of competing futures is insufficient. Preserve a selected destination. An authorized exploratory draft can state one coherent recommendat

ion clearly labeled provisional; use the guided-decision step for incompatible choices within the requested interview scope. Follow the statement with a concise roadmap overview, then the supporting argument.

The reader should understand the distinctive future, why it was chosen and how useful stages make it real. Alternatives-first authoring does not require alternatives-first presentation. Keep the operative brief where it explains consequential choices, not as an interview transcript. Consolidate general caveats while keeping decision-specific limits visible. A concise appendix is optional; do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts or bury all evidence there. There is no vision word ceiling: scale depth to stakes, maturity and uncertainty.

Assess value, usability, feasibility and viability at the destination. Work backward from the ultimate experience to capabilities, foundations and unresolved breakthroughs, then forward through useful horizons. Each horizon needs a beneficiary outcome, independent intermediate value if later stages never arrive, consequential risk reduced, and evidence for advancing or reconsidering. Near horizons have concrete end-to-end demonstrations, exit criteria and failure conditions; an unchanged baseline must fail a new-capability demonstration. Distant horizons retain outcomes, assumptions and provisional conditions with decreasing precision. Qualitative conditions are valid; invent no distant dates, targets or commitments. Retain justified operator timing as aspiration or constraint. Research stages name uncertainty, stopping conditions and enabled value; activity or infrastructure completion alone is not product value.

Connect necessary research, adoption, distribution, funding, partnerships, operating practices and team capability to engineering outcomes. Show dependencies, parallel opportunities, critical path and timing assumptions, including nontechnical prerequisites. Explain components, state ownership, interfaces and instrumentation where they clarify the path; keep tickets outside the vision. Architecture, security, modernization, reliability and performance belong where they enable value, not as mandatory audit categories. Unlimited-resource analysis, if useful, explains which experiments or specialists help and which bottlenecks remain; workers do not imply proportional progress.

Explain endurance and adaptability at the depth risk warrants: durable principles versus current rules, consequential sources of truth, contracts, trust boundaries, execution locations, integrations, maintenance, feedback and human decisions. Use a diagram when it clarifies foundations. Address costly-to-reverse commitments, replaceable boundaries and migration without speculative extensibility. For major assumption failure, say what remains useful, what changes and which decision returns to the operator. Revisit when exit evidence, assumptions or beneficiary evidence changes; proposed destination changes stay explicit.

State how success and failure would be recognized. Use proportionate beneficiary outcome measures and guardrails, necessary baselines and observation limits; targets are not results and activity counts are not success. Map risky assumptions to cheap discriminating experiments and evidence that would change a decision. Research guidance supplies technical-comparison and evaluation detail when consequential.

End with ordered immediate advances tied to the ultimate demonstration and nearer horizons. Explain each observed gap/opportunity, current capability, incremental outcome, timing, dependencies and continuation evidence. Distinguish preserving, extending, investigating/validating and building; uncertain evidence may warrant validation rather than rebuilding. Choose useful priorities, not a quota or duplicate backlog.

## 5. Review and deliver

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/review.prompt.md` before briefing reviewers or repairing findings.** Give independent reviewers their applicable remit and necessary brief/evidence, not the whole authoring workflow by rote. The author owns revisions; reviews remain read-only and advisory. Use one initial pass, one bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification, then report remaining findings without another automatic repair loop. Unavailable capability means disclosed pending coverage, never impersonated review or host reconfiguration. Keep the compact status honest even when review is omitted.

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/delivery.prompt.md` before final validation, status and adoption handoff.** Deliver one usable argument, accurate reviewed-versus-delivered revision coverage and material open decisions. Explain the direction, value, horizons, ordered immediate advances and evidence limits without starting subsequent work.

Owner: Engineering
Status: active

**Applicable when:** any project. Establish or revise an ambitious product vision and an adaptable roadmap through useful technical and nontechnical advances. This is artifact authoring, not implementation planning or autonomous execution.

**Shortcut:** `Envision project` · **Skill:** `wf-envision`

Imagine what this product could make possible for people and why that future matters. Seek relevant financial and nonfinancial value; strategy explains the choices, sacrifices and path from today's reality. Useful horizons make that path credible.

## Scope and working method

Write one coherent vision by default: the existing canonical location, otherwise root `VISION.md`, titled `<Project>: Vision and Roadmap` when new. Honor requested filenames and preserve existing titles, valid material, working references and unrelated edits. Integrate consequential research, citations, assumptions, contrary evidence and open choices into the argument. Full review accounting belongs in the delivery response; the vision keeps a one- or two-line status naming the review date, reviewed revision labels, roles actually run, pending finding count and unreviewed changes, or stating unknown/not reviewed. Identify revisions with dated labels. Explicit project/operator evidence-location instructions override this default. Existing siblings do not authorize new files, overwrite, retirement or silent invalidation. Substantial separately reusable research can justify a companion only with its concrete purpose stated beforehand; honor a single-document request.

A discussion, prompt-writing request or read-only review writes nothing. Authoring and review do not adopt a vision, create lifecycle records or grant implementation, approval, deployment, commit or publication authority. Do not expand network access, run setup or change the environment. External research stays within authorized scope; disclose missing evidence or request necessary access without silently adding network research to a local-only engagement. Preserve operator-owned strategic choices and existing adoption.

Read phase guidance only at the applicable transition below, before its dependent action. These are project-local operating instructions, not vision-output siblings. Retain needed context; reread only if materially changed or unavailable. Missing, unreadable or conflicting required guidance stops that dependent step: report the exact path and conflict or access gap. Do not substitute canonical guidance around local policy, skip the step, invent coverage or automatically run setup/upgrade. Independent authorized work may continue; these core boundaries always apply.

## 1. Establish the brief

Reuse conversation and project context to establish ambition, beneficiaries, desired progress, horizon, constraints and deliverable. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience; ask for a decision-relevant missing example instead of inventing daily use. Explore who adopts, pays for or sustains the product, why now, deliberate non-goals and what failure means only where these affect choices. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income can coexist. A hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Do not require a market choice before helping explore futures.

When the product belongs to an existing organization, establish its role using known company context; the research phase supplies proportional grounding. Distinguish commitments from current positioning. The portfolio may enable a larger future without defining its ceiling. Standalone projects need no company discovery.

With sufficient context, state your interpretation and proceed. Combine genuine blockers, inferred-brief readback and review notice in one brief exchange; defer nonblocking questions as explicit uncertainties. Silence is not selection. Do not impose a questionnaire, twelve-month horizon, unlimited resources, commercialization, cloud, autonomous agents, platform scope or a fixed horizon count.

For new/substantial visions, select advisory product strategy, domain/application workflow, senior architecture and independent challenge coverage. A substantial revision changes purpose, beneficiary, horizons or their order; other edits use affected reviews proportionately. Scale depth by stakes, maturity and uncertainty. Narrowing needs a brief-specific reason, never lower author effort alone; high stakes or uncertainty keep the default unless the operator directs otherwise. Honor explicit scope, additions or omission. State selected roles, consequential specialties and expected effort without invented cost/duration estimates; reuse an explicit scope without another approval. Selected roles need separate independent contexts, or honest disclosure of shared context and missing independence. No chair or consensus process is required.

When revising an existing vision, **read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/revision.prompt.md` before revising it**.

## 2. Ground the need and starting point

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/research.prompt.md` before gathering or assessing evidence.** Build a compact diagnosis of desired progress, obstacles, pivotal insight and timely opportunity. Distinguish observations, interpretations and hypotheses. Repository facts establish capability, not demand; missing primary research permits a provisional vision with visible gaps.

Separate the project's originating problem, binding operator commitments, present implementation/deployment, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor promote a first deployment into permanent destiny. Name new obligations introduced by expansion and consequential decisions for the operator.

Classify relevant capabilities as working, working with limitations, genuinely missing or not yet established. Attribute operating experience separately from reproduced behavior. Preserve demonstrated strengths as foundations; lack of broad evaluation does not make them absent. Carry verified classifications through the draft and immediate priorities, changing them only with new evidence. Resolve consequential inventory/source/draft/reviewer disagreements through targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, without another broad audit.

## 3. Explore, then recommend

When the destination is open, **before drafting the recommended destination**, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainty. Compare product futures, not only engines, packaging, distribution routes or business models. Explain what people do, what the system does, where human judgment remains and what people receive. Give alternatives enough substance to judge fairly; no fixed count, equal-length requirement or exhaustive research is needed. Apply missing and contrary evidence consistently, including to the favored option.

When the operator has chosen the destination, preserve it; do not manufacture alternatives or reopen strategy by rote. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond today's backlog without assuming bigger is better. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices, financial and nonfinancial value, costs, adoption and sustainability. Compare manual practice, competing products, do-it-yourself or doing nothing where consequential. Distinguish a useful benefit from a mechanism that could sustain its value; do not invent an optimum or moat. Enduring usefulness and stewardship may matter more than excluding competitors.

After concrete alternatives make the choice intelligible, guide remaining decisions that would materially change beneficiaries, product responsibility, destination, horizon order or operating commitments, before settling the recommendation or polishing dependent review material. Take one decision at a time in dependency order. Explain why it matters now, credible options through future experiences, effects on outcomes, roadmap and obligations, your recommendation and uncertainty, and reversibility. Invite a choice, combination, deferral or request for evidence; reflect the actual answer and its consequences before the next dependent step. Ordinary engineering details need no strategic interview.

Pause dependent recommendation/review work while such a choice is unanswered; continue useful independent evidence work. Honor exploratory-draft-first/no-interview requests with visibly contingent choices and a provisional draft; return to conversation within the requested scope. Research-dependent deferrals need a useful next test. Explicit acceptance of a recommended direction can select strategy; silence, review agreement or approval of wording alone cannot. Selection alone grants neither adoption nor implementation authority. Keep choices and reasons in the vision and response, not a new decision artifact.

Place inferred choices and remaining uncertainty near the recommendation. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Future capacity is aspiration, not established capability or a guarantee. Missing present proof does not disprove ambition; contrary evidence still matters. Reducing the destination is an operator-owned strategic choice, not a factual correction. A small first advance must support or test the larger future.

## 4. Write the vision and roadmap

Lead the substantive content **summary-first** with one clearly identified, unified vision statement: a concise standalone paragraph expressing the project’s enduring purpose, the future it exists to make possible and why that matters to the people it serves. Make its ultimate meaning specific to this project; a slogan, feature list or blend of competing futures is insufficient. Preserve a selected destination. An authoriz

ed exploratory draft can state one coherent recommendation clearly labeled provisional; use the guided-decision step for incompatible choices within the requested interview scope. Follow the statement with a concise roadmap overview, then the supporting argument.

The reader should understand the distinctive future, why it was chosen and how useful stages make it real. Alternatives-first authoring does not require alternatives-first presentation. Keep the operative brief where it explains consequential choices, not as an interview transcript. Consolidate general caveats while keeping decision-specific limits visible. A concise appendix is optional; do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts or bury all evidence there. There is no vision word ceiling: scale depth to stakes, maturity and uncertainty.

Assess value, usability, feasibility and viability at the destination. Work backward from the ultimate experience to capabilities, foundations and unresolved breakthroughs, then forward through useful horizons. Each horizon needs a beneficiary outcome, independent intermediate value if later stages never arrive, consequential risk reduced, and evidence for advancing or reconsidering. Near horizons have concrete end-to-end demonstrations, exit criteria and failure conditions; an unchanged baseline must fail a new-capability demonstration. Distant horizons retain outcomes, assumptions and provisional conditions with decreasing precision. Qualitative conditions are valid; invent no distant dates, targets or commitments. Retain justified operator timing as aspiration or constraint. Research stages name uncertainty, stopping conditions and enabled value; activity or infrastructure completion alone is not product value.

Connect necessary research, adoption, distribution, funding, partnerships, operating practices and team capability to engineering outcomes. Show dependencies, parallel opportunities, critical path and timing assumptions, including nontechnical prerequisites. Explain components, state ownership, interfaces and instrumentation where they clarify the path; keep tickets outside the vision. Architecture, security, modernization, reliability and performance belong where they enable value, not as mandatory audit categories. Unlimited-resource analysis, if useful, explains which experiments or specialists help and which bottlenecks remain; workers do not imply proportional progress.

Explain endurance and adaptability at the depth risk warrants: durable principles versus current rules, consequential sources of truth, contracts, trust boundaries, execution locations, integrations, maintenance, feedback and human decisions. Use a diagram when it clarifies foundations. Address costly-to-reverse commitments, replaceable boundaries and migration without speculative extensibility. For major assumption failure, say what remains useful, what changes and which decision returns to the operator. Revisit when exit evidence, assumptions or beneficiary evidence changes; proposed destination changes stay explicit.

State how success and failure would be recognized. Use proportionate beneficiary outcome measures and guardrails, necessary baselines and observation limits; targets are not results and activity counts are not success. Map risky assumptions to cheap discriminating experiments and evidence that would change a decision. Research guidance supplies technical-comparison and evaluation detail when consequential.

End with ordered immediate advances tied to the ultimate demonstration and nearer horizons. Explain each observed gap/opportunity, current capability, incremental outcome, timing, dependencies and continuation evidence. Distinguish preserving, extending, investigating/validating and building; uncertain evidence may warrant validation rather than rebuilding. Choose useful priorities, not a quota or duplicate backlog.

## 5. Review and deliver

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/review.prompt.md` before briefing reviewers or repairing findings.** Give independent reviewers their applicable remit and necessary brief/evidence, not the whole authoring workflow by rote. The author owns revisions; reviews remain read-only and advisory. Use one initial pass, one bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification, then report remaining findings without another automatic repair loop. Unavailable capability means disclosed pending coverage, never impersonated review or host reconfiguration. Keep the compact status honest even when review is omitted.

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/delivery.prompt.md` before final validation, status and adoption handoff.** Deliver one usable argument, accurate reviewed-versus-delivered revision coverage and material open decisions. Explain the direction, value, horizons, ordered immediate advances and evidence limits without starting subsequent work.

# Data and Control Flow

Owner: Engineering
Status: active
Last verified: 2026-10-31

## Runtime advisory boundary

`runtime_advisory.py` derives nonblocking advice from the executing interpreter and returns data without printing or changing environment state. `wf_cli.main` owns one stderr notice per command invocation; the executable MCP serving entry in `server.py` owns one per server process. MCP help and dry-run verification stay silent for this notice, preventing a duplicate during setup. Imports, hot reloads, tool handlers and readiness monitors do not emit it.

`setup_readiness.assess_setup` includes the data in `advisories`, separate from reasons and actions. Existing status, startup blocking, text formatting and exit-code decisions remain unchanged. Index health exposes the assessment for agents whose host hides stderr.

## Primary Control Paths

### Optional inference service

`inference_provider.py` reads the distribution-owned `inference_profile.py` for
every selection. The default delegates to the existing Tensorwell client; local-only
selection returns the existing local fallback; an explicit extension loads its
declared flat helper and validates both capabilities before use. Setup and indexing
use the same facade outside MCP. Extension factories and operations receive finite
monotonic deadlines; their trusted transports enforce them, and late or malformed
results are refused with fixed nonsecret errors. No failed extension request retries
another provider. Existing search/lexical degradation still reports unavailable
inference and does not construct a replacement model.

The server reload evicts the facade and declaration with other framework routing
modules, and the existing helper inventory reloads the adapter and reports its source
digest. The profile and facade are explicit members of the core script and setup
source inventories. Implementation reload executes their exact source bytes and
refreshes their launch digests only when pre/post source hashes agree. Before reload,
a changed profile or facade is reported as stale; after reload its current routing is
represented by the updated identity. Model compatibility pins remain bound to the
loaded index runtime and require restart when changed.
Selection and actual execution reuse the existing status fields with a bounded public
provider label. Status itself performs no adapter or network work.

Actual MCP serving enters the FastMCP lifespan and schedules a once-per-process
Tensorwell discovery/start worker; tool registration does not wait for it. The worker
uses a qualified installed controller only for a bounded start of the existing
configuration. Client deadlines terminate/reap only the exact owned CLI child and grant
no authority over the shared daemon. Ready services can also be reused by standalone
index/setup processes, whose imports never initiate startup. Inference selection and
raw query/document roles are specified in [Embedding model](embedding-model.md#optional-tensorwell-execution-wave-20nju).
Compact server-info status reads cached client state without a fresh probe.

Implementation reload refreshes the client in place while preserving its process-owned
locks, startup-once flag and any existing startup worker. It invalidates the qualified
pair cache; discovery or inference from the previous client generation cannot publish
new cached state or return service output. The existing worker keeps its original
deadline, and reload never schedules another start or stops the shared service.

### MCP process lifetime and cleanup

The agent host owns each stdio connection and its server process lifetime.
`wf_reload_mcp` updates the implementation and handler inside that same process;
it does not replace Python or disconnect another session. `wf_server_info` and
reload expose `data.process` with PID, parent PID, project root and monotonic
uptime since the first server implementation import. Uptime survives reload.
The explicit reload result says whether the implementation changed and that the
process was not restarted. Runner changes still require a host restart.

Reload first pauses monitor callback admission under a shared condition and waits
up to one second for active callbacks to drain. Admission and active bookkeeping
use the same condition; callback bodies execute outside it, and their active
interval includes status/error processing. If preparation times out or raises,
the pause is released without stopping workers or disposing handler resources.
The blocked callback continues; ordinary scheduling resumes without a reload.
Preparation refusal reports phase `prepare` and `handler_preserved: true`.
Successful preparation keeps admission paused until cleanup stops the workers.
This budget covers preparation waiting, not the existing public reload tool's
telemetry projection work. It does not quiesce arbitrary foreground tool calls.

The serving lifespan finalizer resolves and closes the current handler, including
a handler installed by reload, on normal exit or serving exception/cancellation.
`ImplHandler.close` attempts the two monitor stops, telemetry close and cache
invalidation independently, clears index references and reports named failures.
Each monitor join waits at most one second; a surviving worker retains its
thread and stop-event references for retry. Reload refuses before module
re-execution or handler replacement when cleanup is incomplete, leaving the same
handler installed. Other independent resources may already have been released;
this is a retryable cleanup failure (phase `cleanup`, `handler_preserved: false`),
not a promise of uninterrupted service. Failures after destructive cleanup begins
are not rolled back; the preservation guarantee applies only to preparation.
Shutdown failures are reported on stderr without replacing the serving error.

EOF regression coverage includes idle serving, repeated reload and finite active
work. It does not promise immediate interruption of arbitrary blocking/native
work or graceful cleanup after SIGKILL. A quiet host-held connection is not proof
of abandonment: Wavefoundry adds no idle killer or cross-session process sweep.
Cleanup never stops Tensorwell's shared daemon or menu application. If cleanup
continues to fail, restart the MCP connection through its host when other work
on that host can be interrupted.

### Lifecycle response completion

The four native create, prepare, implement and close handlers construct their core
response, then pass through `_lifecycle_context_result`. An explicitly declared
`EXTENSION_LIFECYCLE_RESPONSE_CALLBACKS` helper receives detached response/argument
copies at that point, before context-efficiency recording and checkpoint projection.
Its bounded JSON mapping occupies only `data.extension_response`; callback failures
add a bounded advisory without changing core publication truth or retrying writes.

Mutating calls keep their existing project publication hold until completion returns.
Preview retains its existing nonmutating behavior without that hold. An early return
that never reaches completion has no callback; unsupported tools have no late fallback.
Canonical aliases and overrides that delegate to the core reach this boundary once per
core execution. The helper uses the existing declared-source loader, provenance and
reload cleanup; no extra scan, evidence file, approval step or network work is added.
The callback is trusted synchronous code, not a sandbox, deadline or rollback boundary.

### Read-only lifecycle inspection during a retained upgrade

Only the native Prepare `dry_run`/`evaluate` and close-wave `dry_run` paths may inspect a retained upgrade. The registration guard binds the actual arguments and checks the native handler identity; canonical aliases use the same route, while replacement handlers and other publishers retain the guard. A private call context skips the lifecycle lock, completion callback, focus and accounting publication only after bounded checkpoint compatibility and loaded-code checks pass. Validation still runs once; no upgrade continuation, indexing, model startup or checkpoint changes occur.

The checkpoint check accepts supported protocol and legacy memory shapes, extension phase names, and checks repository identities when supplied. It compares installed VERSION with recorded versions and uses the existing loaded-source and ordered runner digest formats through capped no-follow reads. These local read adapters must stay aligned with `setup_readiness`'s source inventory/schema and the runner's two launch files. This proves advisory shape/current-code compatibility, not pack integrity, resume authority or upgraded readiness. Unreadable, incompatible or stale state refuses with `upgrade_preview_unavailable` and preserves the checkpoint.

The child uses `docs-lint --read-only` with bytecode disabled and no inherited cache prefix. This full assessment performs the existing checks but publishes neither scanner findings nor skip observations. Newly detected secret findings are returned as failures with an explicit unpublished notice, so a close preview cannot mistake an unchanged findings ledger for a clean scan. There is no second scan. `--changed`, advisory incremental options and `--write-migration-audit` are incompatible with `--read-only`. Ordinary no-upgrade previews retain their existing observation/callback behavior.

### Path 1: Lifecycle ID Generation

1. Operator mints an ID via the MCP `wf_create_wave` / `wave_new_<kind>` tools (preferred — they dedupe against on-disk IDs), or, when MCP is unavailable, the CLI `python3 .wavefoundry/framework/scripts/lifecycle_id.py --kind wave --slug <slug>`
2. Script reads `docs/workflow-config.json` for the `lifecycle_id_policy` block (`scheme_version`, `epoch_utc`, `offset`, `hour_offset`) once per mint
3. Encodes the base value per scheme — `v2`: `offset + days_since_epoch × 4096 + blake2s-hash entropy(kind, slug)`, min-width-5 base36, no modulo (values past 36^5

widen gracefully to 6 chars); `v1`/absent: `(days_since_epoch × 288 + bucket_5min) mod 36^5`, 5 base36 chars — then linear-probes past on-disk IDs to the final prefix. The on-disk IDs come from the plans root, every candidate wave and archive folder and `docs/architecture/decisions`; minting never mints blind (wave 1zrak): a prefix source that is present but cannot be inspected or listed refuses with `record_root_unreadable` (the plans, waves or archive root, or the decisions directory) or `record_folder_unreadable` (a candidate wave or archive folder), path-free, instead of being read as empty, while a dot-prefixed or symlinked candidate folder it cannot list is skipped, as discovery skips it. The refusal reaches `wf_new_*` and `wf_create_wave` as a structured error, and the CLI prints `lifecycle_id: error: <diagnostic>` and exits 2. The local dashboard's document endpoint answers the same refusal with `503` and the diagnostic.
4. Prints ID to stdout for operator to use in wave or change documents

The `scheme_version: "v2"` policy is provisioned by code, not agents: fresh installs auto-provision via `wf setup` Step 0 (`setup_wavefoundry._provision_lifecycle_policy_if_absent`, repo-root-anchored, absent-block-only); upgrades run `upgrade_wavefoundry.py` Phase 2c (`materialize_lifecycle_policy`) automatically and re-verify at cleanup via the reconciliation backstop; the standalone `wf upgrade --materialize-lifecycle-policy` command is the recovery fallback. All paths are idempotent — a repo already on v2 is never re-provisioned.

**State read:** `docs/workflow-config.json`
**State written:** none (ID is printed only)
**Domain owner of mutation:** operator (manually inserts ID into docs)

1. **Agents:** MCP **`wf_validate_docs`** / **`wf_garden_docs`** call the same `docs_lint.py` / `docs_gardener.py` backends as the CLI launchers. **Hooks / CI:** **`wf docs-lint`** (canonical cross-OS dispatcher subcommand) calls `python3 .wavefoundry/framework/scripts/docs_lint.py`. This repository does not rely on repo-root `./docs-lint`.
2. Linter reads `docs/prompts/prompt-surface-manifest.json`, checks `framework_revision` against `.wavefoundry/framework/VERSION`
3. Validates required prompt docs exist, metadata fields are present, wave/journal roots exist
4. Reads optional `docs/lint-rules.toml` once per invocation through a capped,
   contained no-link read. Its literal `[exclude].paths` list filters only the
   generic metadata and outgoing-link loops in full and incremental lint.
   Existing required-document and renderer policy/protocol registries plus

5. Exits 0 on pass or non-zero with actionable error on failure

The shared incremental full-fallback inventory includes the rules file. Its

Authoring distinguishes originating need, binding commitments, present deployment and possible product responsibility. For an open destination, serious alternatives receive concrete experiences, value, obligations and consistent uncertainty treatment before the recommendation is drafted; a chosen destination is preserved. Current capabilities are classified from source, artifacts and attributed experience and remain consistent through priorities. Research distinguishes source types, dates, limits and contrary evidence; technical shifts need causal evidence and credible alternatives. For products within an organization, briefing and research use relevant mission, portfolio, customer evidence and operating context, separating commitments from public positioning and hypotheses. Existing roles challenge company fit, unjustified ambition limits and cross-product dependencies; company research is conditional and grants no strategic authority. ### Path 8a: Rust Call Provenance and Graph Publication (wave 206og)

Rust extraction reads the grammar's implementing-type and optional-trait fields
separately. Trait methods have identities such as
`src/profile.rs::<Profile as FromStr>.from_str`, while receiver inference uses
`Profile`, including for `Self`. Supported macro token-tree calls retain their
original UTF-8 byte spans; synthetic parse offsets never become repository
locations. Simple loops over explicit array element types use lexical facts
within their own bodies. Unknown shadows and unsupported iterables block an
outer inference rather than borrowing a same-name project method.

Each call occurrence resolves before edge union. The producer preserves its
source file, byte span and one-based byte columns in `call_sites`; an unknown
witness cannot borrow another occurrence's target or precision. Existing edge
keys and confidence remain unchanged, and the JSON attributes hold the sorted,
deduplicated occurrence list. SQLite publication and content fingerprints include
these facts, so an edit that only moves a call still changes the graph content.

Graph builder 54 retires the prior per-file extraction cache and published graph
representation. Ordinary builds re-extract unchanged files at this boundary;
query-triggered rebuilding follows the coordinated build path. Required rebuild
failure remains not-ready. Generation-bound query pins retain their original
nodes and spans while a later build publishes a replacement. MCP projection
copies occurrence data and derives the optional legacy `line` from the first
proven occurrence; it does not scan source for a matching method label. An edge
without supported provenance has an empty occurrence list and no precise line.

## Runtime Lock Convention

Dedicated project-runtime OS-lock carriers live under `.wavefoundry/locks/`:
the dashboard launch mutex and lifetime/metadata carrier, the project-state
publication lock, and context-efficiency producer leases under `locks/producers/`.
`runtime_lock.py` is the mechanical authority for lazy parent creation, binary
open, POSIX/Windows acquire and release, byte ranges, typed busy versus I/O
outcomes, held probing, handle closure, and in-place JSON metadata. Lock files
persist after release; pathname existence never proves a live holder.

Record-style locks (the lifecycle and index-build locks) are open file
description (OFD) locks on Linux and macOS with a 64-bit interpreter on x86_64
or arm64 (wave `1zxnz`), so an unrelated open and close of the lock file in the
holding process cannot release them. Elsewhere, or when the kernel or filesystem
rejects OFD as unsupported, they fall back to classic `lockf`, decided per
acquire; a busy OFD result is busy and never falls back. OFD and `lockf` locks
exclude each other, so older processes stay excluded during an upgrade. Each
lock records its `mechanism` (`ofd`, `lockf`, `flock` or `msvcrt`) and releases
with it. `runtime_lock.py` also owns the per-platform `struct flock` layout, and
holds the in-process hold registry; `wf_reload_mcp` reloads it in place, state
preserved, keeping the registry, its guard and its exception classes, before any
evicted module is re-imported.

Resource wrappers retain policy. Dashboard code owns check → launch-lock →
recheck → spawn → lifetime-lock ordering; review evidence owns same-thread
re-entrancy; context-efficiency owns producer abandonment and reap; the indexer
owns stale-owner, F_GETLK holder-PID, `ended_at`, and interrupted-build
interpretation. `.wavefoundry/index/index-build.lock` therefore remains
co-located with the nuke-and-rebuild index resource, while
`.wavefoundry/upgrade-in-progress.json` remains a root-level transaction/state
marker rather than an OS-lock carrier. SQLite locks intrinsic to their
resource files and the framework test-run lock are outside this path convention.

Upgrade performs a one-way cutover with no runtime fallback. Before extraction,
the new pack's upgrade extension records dashboard restart intent, stops the
installed dashboard, proves the old dashboard/publication/producer carriers are
not held, and deletes those old paths. The extracted runtime recognizes only
`.wavefoundry/locks/`. Cleanup restarts a previously running dashboard on its
prio

r port before removing the upgrade marker; restart failure retains the
marker and intent for recovery. Every creator provisions its own lock parent,
so fresh installs and upgraded projects do not require eager directory setup.

Reporting reads those rows without a second inventory walk; it has no fixed time or byte bound. Run **Review memories** (`memory_backfill(mode="create")`, then `memory_validate`) when you choose to curate history; ordinary incremental indexing refreshes candidates and judgments.

The on-demand run states are `inventory_pending`, `awaiting_validation` and `indexed` (the retained physical terminal label). Setup and upgrade synchronize one advisory inventory and report its existing

publication-lock paths across the deletions; the v1.13 root-lock file is

The ordinary runner checks retained checkpoint/storage authority before checkpoint
